strategies.name: SEASONS

source.prices: Yahoo BTC daily (same series as the shared BTC benchmark / social_paper BTCUSD_yahoo_1d.csv, extended with the lab snapshot)

strategies.costs: 0.10% fee plus 0.10% slippage per side (the site's planned costs)
strategies.fill: Signal on the close, fill at the next close
caveats: New backtest of the site's published season clock on Yahoo BTC daily closes, run from the 9 Jul 2016 halving so 2020 is a complete year. Spring starts on a halving; summer on the first close above the prior cycle's all-time high (max close from the previous halving through the day before this one); fall on a 30% drop from the summer high (cash); winter once fall has lasted 300 calendar days, a 60% drawdown from the summer high has been reached, and the close is above the 50-day average. The site has not frozen exposure for spring, summer or winter; this path is 100% BTC in those phases and cash in fall, with 0.10% fee plus 0.10% slippage per side, signal on the close and fill at the next close. Yahoo's BTC-USD series starts 17 Sep 2014, so the 2013 cycle ATH is the published Bitstamp daily high of $1,163 on 30 Nov 2013; summer starts on the first close above that high (23 Feb 2017). A literal 30% drop from the running summer high put the account into fall on 15 Jul 2017 (from a mid-year high near $2,958, not the later December 2017 peak). From that lower high the 60% winter drawdown was not reached in the 2018 bear (the low stayed above 40% of $2,958), so the book stayed in cash until the 11 May 2020 halving. That is the published rule applied causally, not a hindsight cycle-top overlay.
On 1 Jan 2020 the clock was in fall.
Only a handful of halvings can be tested. Phase rules can be read more than one way; the prior-cycle ATH definition used here is written out in the method note.
The framework was published after much of this history. Exposure for non-fall phases is still not frozen on the site; 100% BTC is a proxy so a curve can be shown, not a launched rule.

strategies.name: S&P 500 dip-buy
strategies.costs: 0.05% per side, added on top of the $1,000 slot at entry and taken from proceeds at exit
strategies.fill: Buy and SMA or time-stop exits at the next session's open; stop filled at the trigger close
caveats: New backtest of the site's exact equity dip-buy rules: signal when the close is at least 20% below the 25-day average (that average includes today's close), deepest discount first, $1,000 slots, up to 10, buy at the next session's open, exit at the next open after a close back at or above the 25-day average, −15% close stop filled at that close, 20-trading-day time stop (counted as closes after the entry day, exit at the next open), 0.05% per side added on top of the $1,000 as in the live engine. Universe is today's S&P 500 list (Wikipedia composition saved with the paper engine), with each name held out until its listed addition date. Companies that later left the index are missing (survivorship bias). Prices are Yahoo, split- and dividend-adjusted, cached in this handoff folder.
Do not treat this as a deployable edge: today's index members are used, so removed losers are missing. The same warning already appears on #9.
This is in-sample.
